subject: Pilot unit-cost reconciliation and next decision points
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@relaybank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot unit-cost reconciliation and next decision points

Hi Ava — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the concrete next steps we agreed on. I wanted to put everything in one place so your procurement and finance teams have what they need.

Key pains you described:
- High per-request latency and spikes during peak ACH batch windows causing customer-facing timeouts.
- Token spend unpredictability across normalization and canonicalization steps in the pipeline.
- Tight Q3 budget: procurement has a $35k/mo cap for new infra pilots.

Goals you shared:
- Proof-of-concept that reduces per-API call cost by >= 40% vs your current baseline while keeping 95th percentile latency under 300ms.
- A pilot that runs in production‑adjacent traffic for 4 weeks and can be scaled to 5M API calls/day.

Recommended pilot scope (summary):
1) Pilot model: mid-sized open LLM (approx 8B) hosted on a dedicated Redwood pool.
2) Cost levers we'll apply: continuous batching for low-latency windows, prefix/KV caching for repeated customer queries, and 4-bit quantization for non-critical steps.
3) Trial connectors: proxy into your staging API, instrument per-route token counters and latency tracing.
4) Duration & gates: 4-week pilot with go/no-go decision after week 3 based on cost per call and latency SLOs.

High-level TCO/estimate (initial):
- Estimated token volume during pilot: ~250M tokens/month (combined input + output).
- Redwood hosted list rate (example): $0.03 per 1k tokens -> ~$7,500/month raw token cost.
- With batching/cache/quantization expected savings: 40–60% -> net expect $3k–4.5k/month.
- Additional Dedicated pool baseline fee (reserved capacity for the pilot window): $6,000 one-time reserve (covers predictable throughput).
- Estimated pilot budget (all-in): $9k–11k for the month. This keeps you well under the $35k procurement cap and leaves room for operational margin.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-scope.pdf (one-pager), relaybank-token-model.xlsx (starter token model).

Asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm procurement's hard cap and whether reserved pool fees are allowed as part of the pilot spend?
- I'll open a HubSpot deal record and a shared Drive folder with the two attachments (links below).
- Suggested next meeting: 30-minute kickoff with engineering + finance on Wed 3/24. Does 10:00am PT work for you?

If you want, I can produce a more conservative cost sheet that assumes 60% of traffic is non-cacheable; happy to run that quickly.

Thanks — I’ll loop in our pricing SME if procurement wants line-item granularity.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0122

Thanks Jasmine — helpful summary. A couple clarifications from our side:
- Procurement confirms the $35k/mo cap for pilots, but they require any reserved or onboarding fees to be itemized; one‑time fees are okay if <= $10k.
- Finance wants a stricter downside case: assume only 20% of traffic benefits from caching for the first 2 weeks (warm-up / cache cold-start). Can you provide the conservative cost sheet you mentioned?

Also looping our Engineering lead, Samir (samir.patel@relaybank.com), who will take the technical kickoff. Wed 3/24 at 10:00am PT works for us.

Jasmine — forwarding the thread so Ben can weigh in on commercial structure and credits. Thoughts:
- If procurement allows up to $10k one-time reserve fee, we can propose a $6k reserved pool + $3k onboarding credit to keep RelayBank comfortable. That keeps their first-month cash outlay lower and preserves margin.
- Ben: can we map the conservative scenario Ava asked for to a guarded price schedule (Tier A: 20% cache benefit, Tier B: 40%+ cache benefit) and show monthly totals? Also confirm whether we can extend a 10% usage credit for the pilot under the standard pilot program.

Also, Jasmine — we should prepare a clear walk-through of how batching will be applied to keep tail latency visible (short deck + checklist). I can take the pricing table and Ben can validate the credit.

Marissa
